item.title: Violence trending downward in Alameda Co. amid investments into prevention programs, data shows
item.description: Despite violence being the leading cause of death for young people in Alameda County, data shows that homicides have been on the decline since 2022, while the rest of California is ticking slightly upwards.

item.title: True love and Disneyland: A 70-year fairy tale
item.description: This is a fairytale love story with Disneyland as one of the main characters! Richard and Cynthia Borrud chose Disneyland for their honeymoon in 1955, visiting about a month after the park first opened its doors.

item.title: How storms fueled by atmospheric river could impact holiday travel, plans across Northern California
item.description: Planning on traveling for the holidays? Here's what to know before you hit the road as a parade of storms take aim at the Bay Area and Northern California.

item.title: 8-month-old baby survives fentanyl exposure after quick action by mother
item.description: An 8-month-old baby is recovering after being exposed to fentanyl, thanks to her mother's quick response. The mother found what looked like a sticker, but it turned out to be a fentanyl wax fold.

item.title: AccuWeather Forecast: Light to moderate rain continues tonight; atmospheric river arrives tomorrow
item.description: A Level 1 system will continue to spread rain tonight across the entire Bay Area. The storm is a Level 2 tomorrow afternoon through Sunday. That's when an atmospheric river arrives with heavy rain at times, gusty winds and even the chance of thunder.

item.title: San Francisco set to have float at Rose Parade 2026 for first time in nearly 50 years
item.description: San Francisco officials say they want the float to be a marketing tool for the city - encouraging to come visit and continue its post-pandemic recovery.

item.title: 92-year-old's bittersweet journey to becoming a New York candy-store icon
item.description: Ray's Candy Store, an East Village institution, is a 24-hour spot famous for its egg creams and other indulgent goodies.

item.title: Computer glitch leads to Bay Area 7-Eleven customers paying 100 times more to fill up
item.description: You should check your bank statement if you bought gas at a 7-Eleven in the past week. Hard to believe, but a $79.34 fill up turned into a $7,934 charge, and the company says it has happened to about 200 customers in the Bay Area and beyond.
